changes.change: Preview: from the 4:12 PM call (the service took 20 to 29 s a reply and the call hung up with the ask-result form open). (1) While Ara is slow, after "Ara's taking a moment" the phone says "Still waiting on Ara" every 10 seconds until she answers, so there is no long silence. changes.change: Preview: the phone keeps reconnecting for 8 minutes (was 5) before giving up on the voice service. While the line is down it says the officer's name and that it isn't giving up, a different line each time ("The line dropped, Pat. Reconnecting you to Ara.", "Still trying, Pat. I'm not giving up on you.", "Hang in there, Pat. I'll keep knocking until Ara answers.", "No signal yet, Pat, but I'm as determined as ever.", "Still at it, Pat. A dead spot won't beat us.", "Not there yet, Pat. I'll keep trying for as long as it takes.", "Still trying, Pat. I won't give up before the signal does.", then "You're back with Ara, Pat."). The lines are made by the key holder's text-to-speech in the phone's stand-in voice when the name is entered, when the app opens and when a line opens, and kept on the phone, so they play with no signal; a phone that doesn't have them yet hears the old recordings.

changes.change: Preview: fixes from Jim's 2:26 PM ET call (plan reviewed by Carverhill first). (1) The audio of every line the app says is kept by the key holder (Cloudflare KV, 30 days): the first phone to need a line waits on xAI text-to-speech, every later fetch of the same words in the same voice is instant. (2) A line not back in 2.5 s gets a second request alongside, and the first to answer plays (five fetches in the call took 8 to 10 s). (3) The campaign question for every entity is fetched ahead when the entity is asked; the after-save line waits 10 s like a form line. (4) No double question: when Ara's side answer already ends with the form's question the app doesn't ask it again, and Ara is told never to end with it. (5) "Are you there?" inside a form is answered by the app alone ("I'm here." and the pending question); "where were we?" and "what are we filling out?" get the form's name, what it still needs and the question. (6) The save-or-details answer needs a clear word; a question or an "okay" inside a longer sentence is no longer a save. (7) A yes or no that Grok puts into the summary or next step is thrown out and the field keeps what it had (the report had saved with Summary "Yes."). (8) A next step without a date gets "When is it due?" alone. (9) A reconnect or unlock with a form open names the form before the pending question. (10) Every text-to-speech fetch is its own activity-log row (time, cached or xAI, whether the second request won) and the conversation's end row sums them up, so the voice's latency can be compared with Grok's.
changes.why: "Look at latest log and tell me your proposed changes" (Jim's 2:26 PM call: "both you and Ara asked me to save it, one after the other", "asking multiple questions at the same time"); "Go"; "log xai text to speech response times separately so we can see if using it has introduced more problems with latency"

Live 11:00 AM: a call no longer ends itself at the unlock (the fresh sound start had cleared the mic wait while the old mic's timer still ran: "mic muted, didn't come back in 45 s" five seconds after a lock, 10:53 AM). The fresh-start-into-every-call experiment is taken out: both 10:52 and 10:53 AM calls still locked 30 s after the tap. Lock = pause and the speaker fix held in all three locks of those calls.

Taken out at 11:00 AM, an experiment: a few seconds into every call, at a quiet moment, the app starts its sound and mic afresh once (the same fresh start that follows a lock), and after any lock it asks for the screen wake lock again. In the 10:39 AM test the phone stopped locking the screen for the rest of the call after the first fresh start, so this may keep the screen on from the start.

Live 11:00 AM: after the phone unlocks, the app starts its sound and mic afresh before the line reopens, so Ara comes back on the speaker the call started on (iOS had brought her back on the earpiece after the lock). If the phone refuses the fresh start, the old sound and mic stay.

Live 11:00 AM: lock = pause. When the phone locks (the page goes hidden) the app closes the voice line 3 s later, so nothing is charged while the phone sits locked, keeps the conversation, and reopens the same conversation by itself the moment the app is back, asking the pending question again, with no drop tone and no Carry on tap (as after a dead spot). Hidden longer than 25 minutes, the call ends with the Carry on card. Replaces the 10:02 AM 45 s wait: the 10:06 AM test showed a locked iPhone mutes the mic and pauses the sound anyway, so an open line only cost money.

Superseded by the 10:16 AM lock = pause: when the phone locks (the page goes hidden) the app keeps the voice line for 45 s and logs what the phone does to the sound and mic, ending the call only if the page stays hidden; the sound and mic waits stretch to the same limit while hidden. Until now the call ended the moment the phone locked (the 9:55 AM pocket test with Auto-Lock at 30 s ended at the lock with the Carry on card, though the screen wake lock had been granted).

Live 11:00 AM: when a conversation can't start because the key holder refuses a voice pass, the end row in the activity log carries the reason ("couldn't start: service_429"), not just "Conversation ended" (four silent ends at 9:37 AM).

Live 11:00 AM, from the 9:03 AM driveway call: (1) a mic muted by the phone now keeps the call for 45 s instead of 6 s, because iOS puts up an "Audio Recording / Stop audio recording?" dialog when the phone locks during a call and the mic is back only after Cancel; whether the screen wake lock was granted, refused or released is logged. (2) An entity said over two lines ("the Idaho entity" then "the PAC") now counts as said; it was dropped as unsaid and the opportunity's own entity (Citizens Alliance C3) stayed on the planned ask and was saved. A required entity with nothing to prefill now shows Not set instead of the first entity in the list. (3) "Let's go add an ask" opens the planned ask form (it was refused as not asked for). (4) The next action in Cultivation is named as the button is, Add planned ask.
Live 7:18 AM: the search box on Contacts, Opportunities and Tasks takes the theme's panel colour. In spooky mode it stayed white (Carverhill's screenshot).

Preview only: a "Hey Ara" start-up address. The app's address ending in #call opens straight onto one big mic (one tap and the conversation starts; the phone only turns the mic on after a tap). Settings has the address with a Copy button and the four iPhone steps: a Shortcut that opens the address, a Vocal Shortcut "Hey Ara" that runs it, allowed when locked. On a first visit the welcome shows instead. The open is logged as "Opened with the Hey Ara start-up address".

Editing a task by name: the exact text wins, otherwise the task sharing the most words (the person's name doesn't count). Until now any one shared word made two tasks "match" and the app asked which one, even with the exact words (three bug reports from the 5:57 PM call).

Scripted lines: when Ara answers on her own while a scripted line is still to play, the app no longer takes her reply for the line starting; if she said much the same thing, the late copy is cut. The task status question ("Mark X as done?") is a scripted line, so she doesn't announce it and then ask it. New Needs attention filter hands_free lists the hands-free saves still to be checked.

The app tracks where a form process stands (an optional question pending, a read-back waiting for a yes, the substantive question, or which required fields are missing). After a reconnect it puts that in Ara's instructions and asks the pending question itself as a scripted line; Carry on hands over the same position.

Heard check: for every line Ara says the phone records the voice audio received, the sound it produced (an analyser on the speaker path) and what the mic heard while it played; a line that fails a reading is logged ("Ara's line may not have been heard: ..."). "Are you there?" logs those readings for her last line, wakes the sound if the phone paused it, and Ara repeats the line word for word.

Scripted lines get 8 s to start before Ara says them herself (was 5 s; five lines fell back in the 4:42 PM call and then played late), and the fallback tells her to say the exact words. A form left open from an earlier conversation is in Right now, so a new conversation knows about it. Log events carry an id and the key holder stores a batch that arrives twice only once (the 4:55 PM log had 20 s of rows doubled).
The dead-spot limit is 5 minutes (Carverhill's choice; it was 10 minutes for twenty minutes, and 2 before that).

In a dead spot the app keeps reconnecting for up to 10 minutes (was 2) and picks the conversation back up by itself when the signal returns; after the first minute down, "Still trying to reconnect" is said every 30 s instead of every 10 s.

A source check guards against a // comment that swallows code on its line (it failed six checks once today): tools/lint-comments.js runs before every publish and as a suite check, which also makes sure every app script parses.

Hands-free is now on from the start of every conversation, for everyone: the assistant reads each finished form back and saves it on the officer's yes, without any tapping. Saying "I've parked" or that you'll tap yourself turns it off for that conversation. Also from the 3:50 PM walk: when the assistant offers the next form in two sentences ("We were about to decide on moving Sandy to Cultivation." then "Want to do that now?"), a yes now opens the form; the guard used to read only the last sentence and refused three times.

From the 3:38 PM walk: a fresh line that didn't open within 10 seconds made the app give up after one try, because the two-minute rule counted from the start of the call while the new line was opening. The clock now runs from when the voice service was last heard, so the app keeps reconnecting through a dead spot.

The phone's built-in speech is no longer used at all. An iOS "Audio Recording / Stop audio recording?" dialog appeared over the app today, muting the mic and ending the call; the first time was within a second of the phone's own voice saying the voice service wasn't answering. Status lines are recordings played through the call's own sound, and the not-answering message is shown on screen instead of spoken.

The evidence rule is now checked exhaustively by the app's own test run: every form, every pick-list option, flag, amount and date (634 cases), each dropped when unsaid and kept in several ordinary phrasings. The table found and fixed three gaps: "in two weeks" (and similar) counts as a date, "half a million" as an amount, and the Event and Email meeting types have word lists.

Preview only: general evidence rule. Every value the voice model puts on a form must be traceable to the officer's own words in the call (amounts in digits or words, entity names, everyday words for each pick-list option, the flag's own word, something date-like for dates). A value with no evidence is left off the form, written in the Voice log, and named to the assistant as left out so she asks instead of reading back a guess. Free text (names, email, summary, notes) is not checked.

Found by the Ara consistency run: the voice model sent an amount of zero on a planned ask, the read-back said $0 and it saved. A money field of $0 now counts as missing: the app leaves it blank, tells the assistant to ask for the real amount, and Save asks for it.

From the 12:41 PM call (five team notes): the campaign question is asked and an entity-worded answer no longer fills it; a repeated optional answer after a dropped line is ignored instead of filled in; the assistant explains that a next step becomes a Task and asks whether to set it, never suggesting the step, date or way of contacting; the call shows Speaking only while sound is actually playing; the phone's own status recording is cut short when the line comes back (no more talking over Ara); and within two minutes of a save a new form opens only on the officer's word, otherwise the assistant offers it in one question first.

From the 12:18 PM driveway call: the call no longer hangs up after 3 reconnects; while the phone is online it keeps reconnecting (with the spoken "still trying" line) and gives up only after 2 minutes without a word from the voice service. When the app drops a capacity rating the officer never gave, the assistant is told, so she can't read it back. Asking for hands-free together with a task no longer gets "What would you like to do?". The Interested outcome is kept only when the officer calls the person interested, keen, positive and so on (consistency rerun: 1 of 10 kept on the word "interest" in passing).

Preview only: an interaction report keeps only what the officer said. If the voice model marks it substantive, picks an outcome or invents a next step the officer never gave, the app leaves those out, tells the assistant so, and asks the substantive question and the next step itself (found by the Ara consistency run: 2 of 6 reports marked substantive by the model, one with an invented next step).

Settings has a switch, off by default, to record the phone's location (to about 10 metres) in the notes about the voice line dropping, reconnecting or ending; the activity page links each spot to a map; the privacy notice says so.

Preview only, from the 10:02 AM call: the reconnect lines are recordings played through the call's own sound (the phone's speech is silent during a call on an iPhone), with "You're back with Ara." when the line returns; when Ara reads a form back herself in full and the officer says yes, the app saves instead of reading it back again; the optional details are led, not offered ("Let's take the next step: a few optional details..."), each field asked as "Fill it in, or move on?"; a rating said before the questions start is taken; "move on" or "no" to a fill-in field skips it; the next-step question says a substantive interaction needs one and suggests an example; after a drop with no form open Ara carries on with the person just worked on; a quiet line that is dead gets a fresh line; a line up for 20 s starts the reconnect count afresh.
Preview only: Settings > Version shows the build stamp as written (iPhone showed Invalid Date).

Preview only, from the 9:06 AM call: a reconnect can no longer hang on fetching a voice pass (each try is limited to 6 s and tried again every 2 s for up to 2 minutes; one took 89 s and the next never came back, so the officer had to end the call); while the line is down the phone itself says "The line dropped. Reconnecting you to Ara." at 5 s, "Still trying to reconnect." at 12 s and every 10 s after; a yes to a read-back saves the form even if Ara opens another form instead of calling save_form, and another form waits while a read-back is unanswered; a move to Cultivation is refused at the save too when the criteria are missing; after a side question Ara repeats her open question in full; activity log batches that fail to send are sent again; the "Opened the app" row names the build.

Preview only, from the 8:25 AM call: a new contact is asked its capacity rating before the other optional details (an opportunity needs it), and "Would you like to add more details?" comes after; Ara's rules say the app reads the form back and asks "Shall I save it?", so she never does it herself; the app asks for a rating when the officer hasn't said one (no invented ratings); naming a state (New Hampshire) picks its only entity, or lists just that state's entities; moving to Cultivation is explained first (the gift officer believes the contact is ready to be pursued for a gift); while a scripted line is pending Ara is told not to say it herself; a late scripted line is cut only when the first telling was heard.

Preview only, from the 7:54 AM call: the app itself asks whether an interaction was substantive (its own spoken question) and never reads a report back without the answer; in hands-free mode the app reads a finished form back as soon as it is complete, without waiting for Ara to ask (she had said "Tap Confirm"); the hands-free line carries its own follow-up question so Ara no longer goes quiet after it; dates are given with today/tomorrow/yesterday so a same-day due date is not called tomorrow; a scripted line that starts late after Ara already said it is cut instead of being heard twice (and scripted lines now get 5 s to start).

Ara works the way xAI's speech-to-speech 3.0 service expects: her instructions are rewritten as short sections and bullets (same rules, easier to follow, so fewer stray asides and shorter read-outs); the app's guidance now travels with each reply request instead of being planted in the conversation as if the officer had said it, so she can no longer read it aloud; lines that must be said word for word (optional-field questions, hands-free read-backs, cancel, undo, go back, the greeting, the hang-up line) are spoken exactly by the app's scripted line; tool results carry only data; and every new reply or instruction update waits until her previous audio has finished playing, which ends the cut-off sentences after form steps.

Preview only, using more of xAI's voice features: a dropped line or Carry on picks up the same conversation on xAI (kept 30 minutes, tool calls included) instead of a summary; the speech recognizer is told to listen for US English and up to 100 key words (contact names, entities, stages); Ara says C.A. as Citizens Alliance and PAC as pack; the hands-free line is spoken word for word by xAI, then Ara carries on (if xAI doesn't play it, Ara says it).

Preview only: on a computer screen the call bar's background band no longer covers the mic at the top of the left menu during a conversation, and in spooky mode the cobwebs sit in the top corners of the page instead of floating in the middle.
Preview only: the rolling pumpkin plays the opening of Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor (the first 7 seconds of the recording Carverhill sent) as it crosses the screen. It used to be silent.
Preview only: the owl now hoots with a real owl recording (from tunetank.com) instead of the phone-made hoot, both the owl that comes by in spooky mode and the "Tap me to hear me hoot!" owl.

Preview only: turning hands-free on or off mid-form, Ara now says "Hands-free is on. I'll read back all the information on the form and save it when you say yes." and then carries straight on with the form's next question (she used to stop and wait). A mic the phone mutes for a moment no longer ends the call; it waits up to 6 seconds for it to come back.

Fixes from a test call: when the iPhone briefly pauses the app's sound (a notification, Siri, another app) the call stays open for up to 6 seconds while the sound comes back, instead of ending; hands-free stays on after Carry on; if Ara talks past a tapped save the app tells her again; every interaction report asks whether it was substantive and the read-back says so; marking a saved report substantive needs a next step and its due date (creates a task); "it's J B" in an email is no longer read as S J B; in the optional questions the officer can go back to a question, an entity named at the amount question goes to the entity, Ara no longer reads the app's instructions aloud and can't jump to the read-back early; after a Carry on Ara never says something on the open form is saved.

Preview only: after a save Ara says in a few words that it's saved (no more "Saved: task saved"), mentions undo only after the first hands-free save of a conversation, and ends by offering the next step ("Next is to record the ask. Want to do that now?") or asking "What's next?". She no longer asks whether to stop.

Preview only: on a computer screen (1000 pixels or wider) the tab bar becomes a left menu with the mic on top, Home shows Needs attention in a wide left column with the other panels on the right, and Opportunities shows the list beside the open opportunity. Phones are unchanged.

Behind the scenes: the code that keeps the voice line alive (reconnects, line tests, stall and quiet detection, asking Ara again) now lives in one place, with all its timings listed together. Nothing changes in how the app behaves.

Faster recovery on a bad line: if Ara hasn't started replying after 4 seconds, the app tests the line then and opens a fresh one if it is slow (it used to wait 13 seconds). If a new line hasn't opened after 5 seconds, a second one is tried alongside and the first to open is kept. After a reconnect Ara says sorry with no Halloween or Christmas aside and asks only the one question still pending. She passes a question to the project team after any yes, can see opportunities closed this year, and hands-free read-backs say "Summary: noted" instead of reading the summary out.

If the officer talks while the line is down, Ara asks them to say it again once she's back, instead of carrying on as if nothing was said. After a reconnect she answers "Are you there?" with a quick yes and carries on with the open form, without "welcome back" or "what would you like to do" (seen at 6:04 PM).

Tuned from the 5:52 PM drive: when Ara doesn't answer, the app tests the line first and on a slow line opens a fresh one right away instead of asking again (re-asks had piled up six late "I'm here"s); on a healthy line it asks once more, then opens a fresh line. A soft tick plays every 4 seconds while Ara is slow or the line is reconnecting. A new voice pass is fetched as soon as one is used, so a second drop reconnects fast (one took 15 s). Ara's instructions list the entities by state so she can't invent one (she offered a Pennsylvania Fed PAC, which doesn't exist).

More resilience from the 5:30 PM drive: a slow connection test no longer triggers a reconnect while the voice service is still sending (that caused an unneeded drop and 'Did you hear me?'); the quiet hang-up waits 30 seconds in hands-free mode, doesn't start while the officer's voice is on the mic, and is called off if the officer answers as it starts (Ara had said goodbye over 'October 24th'). A new opportunity whose entity has a state campaign always asks National or the state before the read-back.

Recovery for two more cases seen on a drive: a drop right after a hands-free save now tells Ara the save went through (she had tried to save again and said the form closed without saving), and a line that goes dead without closing is caught: if the officer is talking and nothing comes back for 5 seconds, or 12 seconds pass in quiet, the app tests the connection and reconnects instead of hanging up. Reconnect tries are spread over about 15 seconds, wait up to 15 seconds for the phone to come back online, and a line that doesn't open in 10 seconds counts as a failed try.

Steadier voice on a weak connection: a voice pass is kept ready during a call so a dropped line reconnects in a second or two; when Ara is slow a soft tick plays after 4 seconds and the app only asks again at 10 seconds; if she then answers twice, the second answer is cut off; each connection reading times a tiny test request. An ask answered with a check in hand or a yes saves as Accepted, and the ask's Response starts blank so Ara must ask.

When the voice line drops mid-conversation (for example while driving), the app reconnects up to 3 times and Ara picks up where she left off, repeating her last question. When Ara goes silent the app asks her up to 3 more times, then reconnects. If nothing works, the phone plays a short falling tone and says the voice service isn't answering, and the form stays open. Connection readings (online or offline, network type and speed where the phone reports them, time since the voice service last answered) and the reason each call ended now go in the activity log. A planned ask for an entity with a state campaign leaves Campaign blank so Ara asks for it.

When Ara goes silent after the app asks her to speak (no reply, or an empty or failed one), the app asks her once more instead of leaving the officer in silence until the 12-second hang-up. Silent replies and voice service errors now go in the activity log.

Ara understands entities said loosely ("the C-3", "Idaho PAC") and asks which one when it could be several; amounts in words ("one hundred thousand") are understood; a new opportunity now has a campaign of interest, asked when the entity has a state campaign (otherwise National is filled in) and carried to the planned ask.

Opportunity record shows one next-step button: Move to Cultivation once every Qualification step is done, otherwise Log interaction (it used to show both).
Check your hands-free saves: each save now starts with the person's name, e.g. "Ruth Abernathy's capacity rated B" or "Ruth Abernathy: Moved to Cultivation".
Christmas mode now has a white background, with evergreen, Christmas red and gold touches (was a dark evergreen night).
Fix links on Check your hands-free saves now name who or what they are for, e.g. "Edit Ruth Abernathy's contact" or "Open the opportunity: Vasquez, Elena - 2026".
After opening a fix link from Check your hands-free saves, Back (or closing or saving the form) returns to the check list.

Check your hands-free saves: each save now has a link to fix it (Edit the contact, Edit the report, Edit the task, Edit the planned ask, or Open the opportunity).
Christmas mode: Santa's "Merry Christmas, ho ho ho" is now a real recording, replacing the computer voice.
Christmas mode: real sleigh bells (a recording) now play for the sleigh, reindeer, gifts and opening forms, replacing the made-up bell sound.

Interaction reports by voice: when Ara never sends the summary, the app now takes it from what the officer said when she asked what was talked about. A next-step due date that is really the meeting date is dropped. Answering "neither" to Ally or Do Not Contact no longer ticks both. The hands-free read-back no longer says ". ." when a form has nothing else to read.

Christmas mode sounds (preview): Santa now says "Ho, ho, hoooo! Merry Christmas!" in a natural voice, and the sleigh, reindeer, gifts and forms opening use fuller sleigh bell sounds. The old phone-made "ho ho ho", which sounded like an owl, is gone.

Christmas mode (try it on the preview now; in the app it is for December): say "Christmas mode" or use Settings. An evergreen look with snow along the header, pine trees, a wreath by the logo and a nativity scene on Home; snow, gifts, elves, reindeer, Santa's sleigh and a Christmas tree come by with their sounds; Santa asks for a tap so sounds can play; sleigh bells as a form opens, a chime on Save, Joy to the World and Santa's "ho ho ho" on Closed Won; Ara becomes a warm Christmas host. From live Grok tests: Grok must pass the meeting date and type, so "yesterday" and "video call" are no longer saved as today and In person. After a meeting, Grok's suggested next step now fits the stage (Move to Cultivation in Qualification, plan an ask in Cultivation).
The spoken overview no longer stops after the Contact stage. After each stage Grok asks "Shall I go on to the next stage?" and continues on yes. Asking it to go straight through skips the questions.

The demo now follows seven more guide rules. An ask can be planned only in Cultivation. Move to Cultivation? opens a decision: move, or Defer with a reason and an optional Reconsider on date (the prompt returns on that date or after the next substantive interaction). Ask responses are Accepted, Countered, Awaiting and Declined. A declined ask needs a reason and closes the opportunity as Closed Lost. New Record gift (Ask Made, outright gift) and Record payment (Commitment) close the opportunity as Closed Won. The Make the ask reminder is due 7 days before the planned date. Accepted or Countered creates a Follow up on agreed pledge task (due in 10 days, a demo default while the interval is open). How it works and Grok's instructions updated to match.

A substantive meeting needs a next step and its due date unless the outcome is Not interested or Referred elsewhere; an ask meeting needs one unless the investor said no. Grok asks for it and Save is blocked without it. The meeting report gains an Outcome field with the guide's six outcomes, and next-step tasks are filed on the opportunity.
